name: Medicare — RET Medicare opt-out
description: Twenty-six steps, one per row of the source procedure: establish the event and the LOB, confirm coverage and the absence of an SPI-CLM record, price the claim as per Medicare, look the service class up to find the rate, enter it, derive our secondary liability, bypass PX_RET with PX_RY and Pay.

steps.name: Identify the PX_RET event and check the event hierarchy
steps.description: Review the events list in the Event Resolution tab to determine whether any other events must be resolved before the PX_RET event, following the established event hierarchy. RET is the claim event for a member who is eligible for Medicare but has opted out of it. If other events are present, resolve those that come before PX_RET first; if no other events are present, proceed. Here every edit is Informational, so nothing stands ahead of PX_RET.
steps.hint: Event Resolution tab → All Edits. Read the severity beside every code before you touch PX_RET.
steps.checklistItem: Identify the PX_RET event and check the event hierarchy

steps.name: Check the Line of Business via Product field
steps.description: Determine whether the claim is ITS-Host or any other LOB by checking the Product field in the Member Information tab. The Product field shows any value other than ITS, such as Local, National or ACA. In this scenario, the Product is Local, so the trainee proceeds.
steps.hint: Member Information tab → Group Information → Product.
steps.checklistItem: Check the Line of Business via Product field

steps.name: Check for VLD/VL and CLM events
steps.description: Determine whether the claim contains a VLD or VL event, and whether it contains a CLM event, by reviewing the Event Resolution tab. If any of these events are present, follow the alternate guidelines; if absent, proceed. In this scenario, the claim does not fire VLD, VL or CLM events, so the trainee proceeds.
steps.hint: Event Resolution tab → All Edits. Look for VLD, VL and CLM among the codes.
steps.checklistItem: Check for VLD/VL and CLM events

steps.name: Verify the services are covered
steps.description: Navigate to the Search tab → Benefits sub-tab and review the benefits on the claim and identify whether the services billed on line 1 are covered. In this scenario, the services are covered — the Benefits sub-tab displays a tip confirming “In this event, the services are covered” — so the trainee proceeds.
steps.hint: Search tab → Benefits sub-tab. Read the coverage tip at the top.

steps.name: Check for an SPI-CLM LL record
steps.description: Navigate to the Search tab → Limited Liability sub-tab and look for an SPI-CLM LL record. The LL records are displayed under the Limited Liability Results field; check the Type field for SPI-CLM. In this scenario the table shows a single record — Type MED, Effective date 02/26/2024, End date blank, Order of benefits “M-Medicare” — so no SPI-CLM record is available and the trainee proceeds.
steps.hint: Search tab → Limited Liability sub-tab → Limited Liability Results → Type.
steps.checklistItem: Check for an SPI-CLM LL record

steps.name: Review claims history for the Medicare deductible
steps.description: Determine whether the Medicare deductible for the year has been met by reviewing the claims history. Navigate to the Search tab → Claims sub-tab and look for any claims where the Medicare deductible was applied; the results table carries the columns Code, Name, From, To, Type, Provider, Bill Type, DCN, Charged, Paid and Status. In this scenario no claims are present in history (all fields show “-”), and the Medicare deductible for the year as per the DOS (3/15/2026) is $283. The Medicare deductible amounts set by CMS can be reviewed via the Medicare Yearly Deductible and Coinsurance workflow.
steps.hint: Search tab → Claims sub-tab. No rows means nothing has been applied to the deductible.
steps.checklistItem: Review claims history for the Medicare deductible

steps.name: Determine the coordination method
steps.description: Determine the method of coordination and make note of it. This is found in the member's benefits on the Search tab → Benefits sub-tab. It decides, at step 21, whether Our Insurance OOP Met may be set to Yes or must be left as No.
steps.hint: Search tab → Benefits sub-tab → Coordination of Benefits → Method of coordination.

steps.name: Review the COB plan-level settings
steps.description: Expand the Plan Level details by clicking the + icon and look for MEDICARE COB HARD NON-DUP. Expanding displays the Deductible, Out-of-Pocket, Coinsurance, COB and Plan options tables. In this scenario the COB table shows: COB BENEFIT RESERVE (ALL, N), MEDICARE COB BENEFIT RESERVE (ALL, N), COB APPLIES (ALL, Y), COB ALLOWABLE EXPENSE (ALL, N), MEDICARE COB APPLIES (ALL, Y), COB PAY & PURSUE (ALL, Y), COB OUT OF NETWORK PAYS SAME AS IN (ALL, N), and MEDICARE COB HARD NON-DUP (ALL, Y).
steps.hint: Search tab → Benefits sub-tab → + Plan Level, then read the COB table.

steps.name: Confirm the claim type
steps.description: Check the claim type from the Claim Data tab → Details sub-tab → Additional Claim Data section → Claim source sub-section, confirming the Claim type field contains Outpatient, Inpatient or Professional. In this scenario the field contains “Professional”, so the trainee proceeds.
steps.hint: Claim Data tab → Details sub-tab → Additional Claim Data → Claim type.

steps.name: Validate the claim
steps.description: Click the Validate button on the claim summary, then proceed to the next step.
steps.hint: Validate on the claim summary bar.

steps.name: Note the Pricing ZIP code
steps.description: Begin pricing the claim as per Medicare by identifying the pricing ZIP code. Navigate to the Provider Information tab and check the Pricing ZIP field. In this scenario, the Pricing ZIP is 10025-9998.
steps.hint: Provider Information tab → Rendering → Pricing ZIP.

steps.name: Open the Pricing sub-tab
steps.description: Navigate to the Search tab and open the Pricing sub-tab to price the claim as per Medicare.
steps.hint: Search tab → Pricing sub-tab.

steps.name: Enter the product (RBRV) and variance (0000)
steps.description: Update the pricing product by changing the Product input box to RBRV and the Variance input box to 0000. Enter the Product first, then the Variance — Get Pricing is refused until both carry the right value.
steps.hint: Search tab → Pricing sub-tab → Member → Product = RBRV, Variance = 0000.

steps.name: Get pricing for the claim
steps.description: Click the Get Pricing button. An additional button appears between the Get Pricing and Reset buttons.
steps.hint: Search tab → Pricing sub-tab → Claim Lines → Get Pricing.

steps.name: Apply the Medicare pricing
steps.description: Click the Apply Pricing button next to Get Pricing. The allowance amount is then shown under the Allowed column — in this scenario the pricing shown on the claim is $120, and the values update to Billed amount $200, Allowed amount $120, and Write-off $80.
steps.hint: Search tab → Pricing sub-tab → Apply Pricing.

steps.name: Confirm the write-off and note the procedure code
steps.description: Determine the write-off by navigating to the Claim Lines tab and checking the Billed amount field. In this scenario the Billed amount is $200 and the allowed amount previously identified was $120, so the write-off is $80. Also note the Procedure code / HCPCS code on the Claim Lines tab, which will be used for the service-class lookup.
steps.hint: Claim Lines tab → Billed and Procedure. Write-off = Billed − Allowed.
steps.checklistItem: Confirm the write-off and note the procedure code

steps.name: Open Fully Manual cost-share calculation
steps.description: Click VAU/Semi-Manual/Fully Manual from the Action menu to calculate the Medicare-as-primary cost share details — in this scenario, select Fully Manual. VAU and Semi-Manual are shown beside it and do nothing.
steps.hint: Action menu → Fully Manual.

steps.name: Look up the service class and Medicare pay rate
steps.description: Search with the procedure code / HCPCS code noted earlier on the Search tab → Code Set sub-tab and review the service class for the billed service. In this scenario the service classes shown are CL2 (COVID19 LHO BH CODES), CR3 (COVID19 TELEHLTH BH CODES), CR7 (NY COVID19), CT2 (GT MODIFIER FOR TELEHEALT), 08A (PSYCHOTHERAPY), 08C (BHA/MHN PSYCHOTHERAPY), 47C (POSSIBLE TRANSGENDER PROC) and 51M (MH UW PREMIUM PROGRAM). Check whether any service class is 40 or 41: Service Class 40 is paid at 100% of the allowed amount, Service Class 41 is a Medicare Deny, and all other service classes are paid at 80% of the allowed amount. In this scenario no service class is 40 or 41, so the CPT/HCPCS code is covered by Medicare and the pay amount as per Medicare is 80%.
steps.hint: Search tab → Code Set sub-tab. Check every service class against the 40 / 41 / other rate table.
steps.checklistItem: Look up the service class and Medicare pay rate

steps.name: Validate before entering the pay percentage
steps.description: Click the Validate button to confirm the service-class review before entering the Medicare pay percentage.
steps.hint: Validate on the claim summary bar.
steps.checklistItem: Validate before entering the pay percentage

steps.name: Enter the Medicare pay % as 80
steps.description: Open the Claim Lines tab and enter the Medicare pay percentage determined in the previous step — 80 — in the Medicare pay % field. In this scenario the 80% is entered for one claim line, and the trainee proceeds.
steps.hint: Claim Lines tab → Medicare pay % → 80.

steps.name: Update Our Insurance OOP Met to No
steps.description: Review the coordination method identified earlier and update the Our Insurance OOP Met field. If the coordination method is Standard, Carve Out Option 1, or Carve Out Option 3, set the field to Yes or No as applicable; for any other coordination method, leave the field as No. In this scenario, the trainee sets Our Insurance OOP Met to “No” as per the coordination method.
steps.hint: Claim Lines tab → Our Insurance OOP Met → No.
steps.checklistItem: Update Our Insurance OOP Met to No

steps.name: Get secondary benefits
steps.description: Navigate to the Action Menu and click Get Secondary Benefits. The system calculates and populates the secondary benefit information, and the claim lines update to: EOB 00066 with a write-off of $80, EOB 00055 with a non-covered amount of $96, and a payment of $24.
steps.hint: Action menu → Get Secondary Benefits.

steps.name: Hold the amounts with Fully Manual
steps.description: From the Action Menu, click Fully Manual to hold the 00055 $96 amount and allow the payment recalculation, keeping the $24 payment. Verify that the changes have been retained successfully.
steps.hint: Action menu → Fully Manual, a second time.
steps.checklistItem: Hold the amounts with Fully Manual

steps.name: Apply the PX_RY bypass code
steps.description: Complete the final PX_RET event processing: in the Bypass Codes section of the Event Resolution tab, select the PX_RY bypass code to bypass the PX_RET event.
steps.hint: Event Resolution tab → Bypass Codes → Bypass code → PX_RY.

steps.name: Validate the bypass code
steps.description: Click the Validate button on the claim summary to apply the bypass code. Validate is refused while any code other than PX_RY is selected.
steps.hint: Validate on the claim summary bar.

steps.name: Submit Pay decision
steps.description: Once the correct details are updated, navigate to the Decision section in the header, select 'Pay' from the dropdown menu and click Submit.
steps.hint: Decision → Pay → Submit.
